description: Check the DNS records of this mailbox's sending domain (the part after the @) now, instead of waiting for the daily check. The result is saved on every mailbox in the workspace on that domain. SPF and DMARC decide passing or failing; for a send-only mailbox, DMARC alone does. SPF passes only with exactly one record, and when checking this mailbox's mail takes at most 10 DNS lookups (`domainAuth.spfLookups`). Receiving servers check SPF in order and stop at the first match, so we count the terms up to and including the mail provider's include, with every lookup inside it, or the whole record when we don't know that include. We count without a real message, so this is the path the provider's mail takes, not a test of one. DKIM is only found or not verified, because DNS can't list its selectors. When SPF or DMARC fails, `domainAuth.dnsHost` names the DNS provider that holds the domain's zone, in the shape list_tracking_domains describes; it is null otherwise, and when DNS did not answer. If SPF or DMARC keeps failing for 72 hours, warmup and campaigns don't send from these mailboxes until it passes. `domainAuth.records` lists the records for this mailbox: `step`, `type`, the full `name`, `nameInZone` relative to `dnsHost.zone` (`@` at the zone itself, null when unknown), `value`, `priority`, `check`, `observed`, `replaces` and `reason`. There is no SPF row for a send-only mailbox, and no DMARC row while a record on this domain or a parent covers it. If `check` is `unanswered` or `not_checked`, call check_mailbox_domain again before changing DNS. Publish only rows with `check: not_verified` or `wrong` and a non-null `value`, using your own DNS access, then check again. When `replaces` lists records, publish `value` in their place: edit the one record there, or delete them and add `value`, so the name keeps one SPF record and one DMARC record. Never publish a null `value`. `reason` says why it is null: `include_unknown` (ask the mail provider for its SPF include), `too_many_lookups` (remove includes for services the domain no longer uses, or put the mail provider's include first) or `cannot_merge` (join the SPF records into one by hand). A broken DMARC record is replaced with `p=none`, never anything stricter; never replace a working policy with a weaker one. Set up DKIM at the mail provider. We never take a DNS password or token.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

name: check_mailbox_domain
title: Check a mailbox's sending domain
